papers.title: Budgeted Admission from Timestamped Capacity Records in Shared Clusters
papers.abstract: A cluster admission gate can receive a capacity record that no longer matches current schedulability. We study one exogenous binary schedulability unit under a bound on the joint probability of admission and unavailability. For a symmetric Markov state, we derive the stationary admission frontier for a fixed observation delay and apply finite likelihood allocation to a delay-tagged delivered record. A one-sided exact binomial endpoint calibrates each fitted policy, and exact enumeration confirms the per-policy confidence target in every tested parameter cell. A separate deterministic guard charges every unresolved admission against the realized allowance and bounds unavailable-state admissions at every prefix under truthful outcome feedback. An executable admission procedure composes the allocation and guard. The controlled system binds source sampling, NATS delivery, randomized admission, Kubernetes objects, and API-derived outcomes in one append-only record. Independent audit finds no missing event, identity mismatch, or state mismatch in the completed functional block. A separate CPU request-accounting check preserves Job and Pod identity across an unschedulable-to-complete transition.

papers.title: Improved rapid phase ordering for Ising dynamics on random regular graphs
papers.abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs with $n$ vertices at low temperature, in the regime $\beta \geq C/d$ where $C,d$ are sufficiently large constants. In this regime, the full mixing time is exponential in $n$, because of the bottleneck between the two dominant phases: configurations with a majority of plus spins and configurations with a majority of minus spins. We show that, for sufficiently large $d$, if the dynamics is initialized with an excess of at least $\epsilon_{C,d} n$ plus spins over minus spins, then it quasi-equilibrates in time $O(\log n)$ to the Gibbs measure conditioned on positive magnetization. In addition, the required bias $\epsilon_{C,d}$ can be chosen so that $\epsilon_{C,d}\to 0$ as $d,C\to\infty$. Previous bound of \cite{GSS25+} in the Ising and large-$d$ setting required $\beta \gtrsim (\log d)/d$. A key difficulty is that, even from the all-plus initialization, one must control the propagation of negative information in spacetime in a low-temperature model with strong local correlations. We address this by developing a new bootstrap approach to proving subcriticality of disagreement clusters under the grand coupling.

papers.title: Birthday Estimators Are Uniformly Optimal for Renyi Entropy
papers.abstract: Collisions are a basic probe of unknown distributions, used for testing and for counting substructures in graphs, and they underlie R\'enyi entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty with applications in cryptography, machine learning, physics, and biology. Motivated by this, we study the natural birthday estimator. We prove Bernstein-type concentration for it and show that it is minimax optimal, uniformly and jointly in alphabet size, order, accuracy, and confidence, with no sample splitting, clipping, or median aggregation. This, in particular, settles the sample complexity of integer-order R\'enyi entropy estimation up to absolute constants in all regimes, closing the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds. Our concentration bound rests on a sensitivity analysis of collision count, and the matching lower bound on a sharp analysis of detecting a hidden spike in a plateau distribution.

papers.title: Solving the Ho--Nguyen Conjecture for Gaussian Mixtures: Applications to Mixtures of Experts
papers.abstract: Over-fitted Gaussian mixtures can contain many parameter configurations with nearly the same density, making the order of density cancellation central to their parameter-learning rates. Ho and Nguyen encoded these cancellations in a polynomial system and conjectured its exact order as a function of cluster size. The key to resolving the conjecture is a common positive-variance shift that turns the coefficient equations into Gaussian moment matching. For every cluster size $\Mhn\ge2$, we prove that the real, nonzero-weight system has order $2\Mhn$: a sharp sign-change bound forces rigidity at that order, while positive Gauss--Hermite quadrature constructs a non-trivial solution through order $2\Mhn-1$. Population-density calculations at 110-digit working precision recover the predicted leading term for two to six components; finite multistart searches recover the same observed powers for two to five components, with smaller finite-scale constants for three to five components. For parameter learning, the exact order gives an explicit pointwise maximum-likelihood exponent and an exact local minimax order on specified shrinking neighbourhoods of a fixed known mixing measure. The same coefficient viewpoint separates high-order cancellation from exact parameter symmetries in mixtures of experts. Synchronized replication preserves the conditional density while keeping the corresponding parameter losses positive in two broad standard-softmax classes, showing why statistical rate arguments must account for exact parameter symmetries.

papers.title: Density Evolution for Stochastic Dynamical Systems Driven by {\alpha}-Stable Processes: An Equation-Free Numerical Approach
papers.abstract: While well-established approaches exist for computing probability densities of stochastic differential equations driven by Brownian motion, computing probability densities for general stochastic differential equations driven by {\alpha}-stable processes remains challenging, and few general-purpose methods are available. A major difficulty is that the corresponding Fokker--Planck equations governing the density are generally unavailable in explicit form. In this paper, we develop an efficient approach to compute probability densities for stochastic differential equations driven by {\alpha}-stable processes without relying on Fokker--Planck equations or any other governing equations. The proposed approach is easy to implement and computationally efficient. Numerical examples demonstrate its effectiveness and indicate an approximately first-order convergence rate with respect to the time step.

papers.title: Beyond exponential tilting: sharp asymptotics and improved importance sampling for rare events
papers.abstract: A classical approach for importance sampling (IS) of a rare event is to tilt the measure using its large deviation minimizer, thereby shifting the proposal mean towards the event set. While this tilt is log-efficient, we show that the coefficient of variation of the resulting estimator still grows like $\varepsilon^{-1/4}$ in the small-noise limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Motivated by sharp large deviation asymptotics and the local geometry of the event set at the minimizer, we propose improvements using a control variate or an anisotropic, non-Gaussian proposal. We prove, up to truncations that hold with high probability, and confirm empirically in high-dimensional examples, that the former bounds the coefficient of variation and the latter makes it vanish, so that a bounded number of samples suffices. Our analysis addresses both the coefficient of variation of the different proposals and their necessary and sufficient sample size based on the Kullback--Leibler divergence of the IS target from the proposal; both yield the same rates in $\varepsilon$. We demonstrate the resulting samplers, including a variant that blends the classical and the new proposal across noise levels, for a stochastic Korteweg--de Vries equation with thousands of random inputs.

papers.title: Annealed correlation and quenched noise sensitivity in biased deep neural networks
papers.abstract: In earlier work by Jonasson, Steif and Zetterqvist (2023), fully connected deep neural networks with layers of width $n$, i.i.d.\ standard Gaussian weights, sign activations and no bias terms were shown to be annealed and quenched noise sensitive with respect to any joint probability distribution $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}$ on the input $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ and its perturbation $\boldsymbol{\eta}$ satisfying a mild positive-correlation condition and $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbol{\eta} \in \{\boldsymbol{\omega},-\boldsymbol{\omega}\}) \to 0$. Here we add independent Gaussian biases of the natural order and show that quenched noise sensitivity is retained over a broad range of depths, indeed under the slightly weaker assumption that $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbol{\omega} = \boldsymbol{\eta}) \to 0$. Thus, subject to the positive-correlation condition, quenched noise sensitivity holds under the minimal requirement that the perturbed input is asymptotically unlikely to coincide with the original input. At the same time, the annealed covariance remains bounded away from zero and is entirely accounted for by fluctuations in the network-dependent output means.

papers.title: Kernel-based collocation methods for Heath-Jarrow-Morton models with Musiela parametrization
papers.abstract: We study kernel-based collocation methods for numerical solutions of Heath-Jarrow-Morton models in Musiela parametrization. The methods are Euler-Maruyama approximations of finite-dimensional stochastic differential equations and can be used with standard Monte Carlo procedures for derivative pricing. We give a conditional mean-square error estimate under explicit stability assumptions on the differentiated cardinal basis over the full evaluation region required by the volatility functional. The estimate uses the spatial-radius exponent dictated by the squared-error calculation. Two finite-resolution examples illustrate the method for a Vasicek model and for caplet pricing.

papers.title: Four Function Theorems Through Optimal Transport and Entropic Analogs
papers.abstract: We study entropic versions of four-function inequalities and give transport proofs of the Euclidean Ahlswede-Daykin theorem and a four-function version of the Prekopa-Leindler inequality due to Cordero-Erausquin and Maurey. One of our main results shows that the sharp range for the four-function inequality for equally weighted power means of finite orders \(\alpha,\beta\) is \(0\leq\alpha+\beta\leq2\), with the Ahlswede-Daykin min-max inequality obtained as a limit. En route, we prove corresponding entropy inequalities under the quadratic optimal transport coupling, including an entropy power inequality for the minimum and maximum in Euclidean space. We also study the stability of four-function inequalities under convolution with log-concave product densities, recovering the preservation of log-supermodularity established by Karlin and Rinott, and explain its application to a conditional entropy power inequality for log-supermodular random variables.

papers.title: A General Kernel Framework for Non-CND Distance Measures Using |D|-Dimensional Sparse Landmark Embeddings
papers.abstract: Kernel methods, and Gaussian Processes (GPs) in particular, require a Hilbertian distance measure---one whose square is conditionally negative definite (CND)---to guarantee positive semi-definiteness (PSD) of the kernel matrix; a condition that fails for many natural input spaces, including smooth manifolds and spaces of probability distributions. We propose the Sparse Landmark Embedding (SLE) kernel, which eliminates this requirement entirely. Each input is embedded into a sparse feature vector via compactly supported bump functions centered at all |D| training points; applying any standard PSD kernel in this embedding space yields a kernel that is provably PSD for arbitrary distance measures. The compact support automatically controls embedding sparsity, keeping kernel matrices well-conditioned and computationally tractable despite the high ambient dimension. We provide theoretical guarantees on PSD, sparsity, stability, and universal approximation, and show that the SLE kernel matches or substantially exceeds domain-specific baselines in both predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification using geodesic and Wasserstein distances.

papers.title: Explicit Steady-State Approximations for Parallel Server Systems with Heterogeneous Servers
papers.abstract: We study the steady-state performance of parallel-server systems under an immediate routing architecture with two sources of heterogeneity: server types and job classes, often subject to compatibility constraints. We focus on the weighted-workload-task-allocation (WWTA) routing policy, a load-balancing scheme known to be throughput-optimal for such systems. Under a relaxed complete-resource-pooling (CRP) condition, we prove a strong form of state-space collapse in heavy traffic and that the scaled server workloads jointly converge in distribution to a deterministic vector multiplied by an exponential random variable, whose mean is explicitly given by system primitives. Our analysis yields three main insights. First, the conventional heavy-traffic assumption of a unique static allocation plan can be dropped; a relaxed CRP condition suffices. Second, the limiting workload distribution is shown to be independent of the local scheduling policies at the servers, allowing substantial flexibility. Third, the inefficient (non-basic) activities identified by the static allocation problem are proved to receive an asymptotically negligible fraction of routed jobs and service effort, even though WWTA has no prior knowledge of which activities are non-basic, highlighting its robustness to changing arrival rates.

papers.title: Percolation in the Stochastic Block Model
papers.abstract: The stochastic block model is a paradigmatic model of networks with community structure. Yet percolation in the model has been studied primarily in cases with a fixed block structure, even though in real networks, the community structure may evolve as the network grows. Here we study percolation in sequences of stochastic block models in which the numbers and sizes of communities, as well as the intra- and intercommunity connection probabilities may all change with the network size. We analyze five such sequences using two methods: linearized self-consistent equations for the locally tree-like models and a branching process at the community scale for the models with nonvanishing clustering. We find that the critical average degree is not generally equal to $1$, even in locally tree-like sequences, because the transition depends on how connections are distributed across the evolving community structure. We also show that the community-scale branching process accurately predicts the transition when intercommunity connections are sufficiently sparse, even in the presence of nonvanishing clustering, while a geometric stochastic block model sequence demonstrates the limitations of this method when correlations between intercommunity connections cannot be neglected. These results extend percolation studies in the stochastic block model to more realistic scenarios with evolving community structure, and may provide new methods to derive the upper and lower bounds for the percolation threshold in geometric long-range percolation.

papers.title: Vanishing transport noise enhances stability of stratified Couette flow in the 3D Boussinesq system
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the enhanced nonlinear stability of stably stratified Couette flow in the three-dimensional Boussinesq system driven by a common affine Stratonovich transport noise. Our main result shows that, for fixed $\beta>1/2$, suitably chosen noise amplitudes enlarge the range of perturbations for which we prove stability, even as they vanish with viscosity. For each fixed deterministic Sobolev perturbation satisfying the sufficient smallness conditions, the strong solution is global and obeys stability estimates on an event of prescribed high probability. No spatial localization or vanishing initial double means are required. The proof combines noise-induced mixing with coupled energy estimates to control nonlinear feedback and preserve the physical damping of the fast vertical velocity and temperature.

papers.title: A mean value formula for the p-Laplacian
papers.abstract:
In this paper we introduce an asymptotic mean value formula of the form $u(x) - \B_\epsilon^p (u) (x) =\epsilon^2 \Delta_p u(x) + o(\epsilon^2)$ for the $p-$Laplacian, $\plap u := 
abla \cdot  ig( |
abla u |^{p-2} 
abla u  ig)$. Here $\B_\epsilon^p (u)$ is a nonlinear expression that involve the mean value and the surmemum/infimum of $u$ in suitable balls. This asymptotic mean value formula allows us to characterize viscosity solutions to equations with different homogeneities in different sets of variables, like $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=f(x)$ (for $x=(x',x'') \in\mathbb{R}^d$, $x'=(x_1,...,x_n)$ and $x''=(x_{n+1,...,x_d})$), and the parabolic $p$-Laplace heat equation $\partial_t u (x,t)-\Delta_p u(x,t)=0$. Moreover, the resulting asymptotic mean value formulas are related to two-player zero sum games whose value functions, characterized as the unique solution to the corresponding dynamic programming principle, converge as the parameter that controls the size of the steps in the game goes to zero, to the unique viscosity solution to the corresponding boundary value problem for the operator under consideration. Finally, we also include a Holder regularity result for $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=0$ proved using the game theoretical interpretation of the problem.

papers.title: One-Ring Bourgain Alternative And A 5-Decimal Bound On The Dimension Of Harmonic Measure
papers.abstract: Improving theorems of Bourgain and Badger--Genschaw, we prove that the Hausdorff dimension of harmonic measure on any domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\mathbb{R}^4$, and $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geq3$ is at most $3-10^{-5}$, $4-10^{-7}$, and $n-(n-1)^{-(2n+6.12\sqrt{n})}$, respectively. The previous bounds in dimensions $3$ and $4$ were $3-10^{-15}$ and $4-10^{-26}$, while Bishop conjectures that the sharp bound is $n-(n-1)^{-1}$. The main difficulty in optimizing Bourgain's method is estimating non-additive $s$-dimensional Hausdorff-type contents when $s<n$ is close to $n$. Previous arguments used net contents associated to a fixed $m$-adic lattice, with $m$ large depending on $n$. We redevelop the dimension theory using pairwise disjoint cubes in general position and obtain a new estimate showing that one thin ring without large holes surrounding a cube makes it unlikely for Brownian motion to reach the cube before exiting the domain. A key feature of the construction is that the holes are round rather than rectangular. We also propose ten challenges on the dimension of harmonic measure that may provide accessible targets en route to Bishop's conjecture.

papers.title: Matrix divisors, Christoffel transformations and symmetric $d$-connections
papers.abstract: The Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ relates elementary bundle modifications to gap probability recurrences. The moment matrix determines normalization and the splitting type. We define the source and target moduli problems by their local data. The modifications identify common stable loci and conjugate their point-addition maps. For Pearson ratios $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\deg d=1,2$, we construct rational spectral coordinates and compute the induced transformation. For positive even weights with finite moments, reweighting configurations yields the transformed gap probability recurrence. Its coefficient is a rational function of the transformed spectral coordinates. A local formula applies outside these charts under the stated hypotheses.

papers.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
papers.abstract: The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. Solving a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig, this paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential, in any dimension $d\ge 2$. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fr\"ohlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation. This PDUC is established via a bootstrap argument and a key probabilistic lemma proved by adaptively revealing the random potential.

papers.title: Probabilistic Stability Transfer for One-Dimensional Euler Characteristic Transforms
papers.abstract: The Euler characteristic transform (ECT) is a computable topological signature for shapes embedded in Euclidean space. Existing ECT stability results control changes in the transform through deterministic geometric perturbation bounds, but many data-generating mechanisms produce perturbations that are random and unbounded in the worst case. In such settings a uniform deterministic bound may be unavailable or too pessimistic. This paper formulates a probabilistic stability-transfer principle for one-dimensional ECT stability: a deterministic stability estimate is combined with a tail bound for the induced geometric error to obtain a high-probability ECT error bound. We instantiate this principle using the stability theorem of Marsh and Beers for embeddings of finite one-dimensional CW complexes. The resulting consequences cover ambient displacement fields conditionally on admissibility and supremum-tail estimates, and finite landmark perturbations with reconstruction. For landmark perturbations, bounded, sub-Gaussian, sub-exponential, and polynomial-tail noise assumptions give explicit high-probability ECT stability bounds. The framework isolates a geometric stochastic component that arises in shape analysis pipelines across biological morphology, medical imaging, molecular structure analysis, and remote sensing.

papers.title: A Pittel-type limit law for the largest component of random $d$-uniform hypergraphs: enumeration and excursions
papers.abstract: Let $H_d(n,M)$ be a $d$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices and $M$ hyperedges. In the critical window $M=\frac{n}{d(d-1)}(1+\lambda n^{-1/3})+O(1)$, its largest component $L_n$ satisfies $$n^{-2/3}L_n\xrightarrow{\mathcal L} \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}\bigl((d-1)^{1/3}a,\lambda(d-1)^{-2/3}\bigr).$$ (Here $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}(x,\mu)$ denotes the limiting law of the largest component of the critical random graph established by Pittel (2001).) The proof rests on two pillars. First, a bivariate exponential formula gives the exact finite-size law of $L_n$. Subsequently, cancellation of the orders $n,n^{2/3},n^{1/3}$ in the tree normalization determines the series of rooted hypertrees, then that of unicyclic components and its singular expansions at the radius of convergence $\rho_d$. These calculations are exact; they serve the fixed-excess identities and the cancellation mechanism, and nothing more: no unproved uniformity in the excess enters the proof of the limit law. Next, by exploration and martingale approximation, the ordered sizes converge unconditionally to the excursion lengths of a Brownian motion with parabolic drift. A monotone coupling transfers the law to $H_d(n,M)$. The limit law is then identified with Pittel's law by a Brownian rescaling: if $h=d-1$, it suffices to multiply lengths by $h^{-1/3}$ and evaluate at parameter $\lambda h^{-2/3}$. The exact Poisson representation dispenses with any separate deconditioning. We also formulate a two-regime $d$-uniform Bollobas bound (Wright for fixed $\ell$, global combinatorial beyond that), and explicitly indicate why neither regime alone suffices to close the analytic route.

papers.title: Szarek and Ball made simple
papers.abstract: We present proofs of Szarek's moment comparison and Ball's cube slicing inequalities based on elementary convexity and majorisation. The key ingredient is a moment-lifting argument which allows us to use Schur monotonicity, avoiding the integral inequalities used in the original Fourier-analytic approaches.

papers.title: On spatially irregular ordinary differential equations and a pathwise volatility modelling framework
papers.abstract: This thesis develops a new framework for modelling price processes in finance, such as an equity price or foreign exchange rate. This can be related to the conventional Ito calculus-based framework through the time integral of a price's squared volatility, or `cumulative variance'. In the new framework, corresponding processes are strictly increasing, solve random ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and are composed with geometric Brownian motion. The new framework has no dependence on stochastic calculus, so processes can be studied on a pathwise basis using probability-free ODE techniques and functional analysis. The ODEs considered depend on continuous driving functions which are `spatially irregular', meaning they need not have any spatial regularity properties such as Holder continuity. They are however strictly increasing in time, thus temporally asymmetric. When sensible initial values are chosen, initial value problem (IVP) solutions are also strictly increasing, and the solution set of such IVPs is shown to contain all differentiable bijections on the non-negative reals. This enables the modelling of any non-negative volatility path which is not zero over intervals, via the time derivative of solutions. Despite this generality, new well-posedness results establish the uniqueness of solutions going forwards in time. Motivation to explore this framework comes from its connection with a time-changed Heston volatility model. The framework shows how Heston price processes can converge to a generalisation of the NIG Levy process, and reveals a deeper relationship between integrated CIR processes and the IG process. Within this framework, a `Riemann-Liouville-Heston' martingale model is defined which generalises these relationships to fractional counterparts. This model's implied volatilities are simulated, and exhibit features characteristic of leading volatility models.

papers.title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
papers.abstract: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $\theta=\beta/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $N\theta\to\gamma>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/\theta$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $\gamma$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $\beta$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $\gamma\to\infty$.

papers.title: A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs
papers.abstract: We study the graphon variational problem that governs lower tail large deviations of the number of copies of a fixed nonbipartite graph $H$ in a sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph. Our main new insight is that any non-constant minimizer of the variational problem exhibits a discontinuous jump away from the constant graphon. We deduce that the replica-symmetric and symmetry-breaking regimes are separated by a single critical parameter and that the phase transition is first order. In the supercritical regime $p \gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, we transfer these results to the conditioned random graph, showing that the edge density is a discontinuous order parameter and that the conditioned graph concentrates in cut distance near the full minimizer set.

papers.title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
papers.abstract: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.

papers.title: Payoff Polarization and Garbage Concentration in a Stochastic Garbage Disposal Game
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic garbage disposal game on a finite graph in which agents transfer garbage through pairwise interactions governed by payoff-dependent Fermi probabilities. We investigate the long-term behavior of both payoffs and garbage distributions. We prove that payoff dispersion grows at least linearly in time almost surely, leading to payoff polarization, with the maximum and minimum payoffs diverging to positive and negative infinity, respectively. Moreover, the payoff range grows at least on the order of the square root of time. For garbage dynamics, we establish almost-sure concentration on a single agent in the two-agent case for any positive disposal efficiency. When disposal is complete and the underlying graph is connected, we further prove that all garbage becomes concentrated on a single agent after a finite random time, although the agent holding the garbage may change over time. These results characterize the emergence of payoff inequality and garbage concentration in stochastic competitive interactions on networks.

papers.title: An Aldous-type tightness characterisation for the $M_1$ topology: replacing global modulus control by local control at stopping times
papers.abstract: Aldous' criterion provides a stopping-time characterisation of tightness in Skorokhod's $J_1$ topology and is one of the standard tools for proving functional limit theorems. For the weaker $M_1$ topology, where limiting jumps can be approximated by clustered jumps or steep continuous motion, no analogous characterisation has been available and tightness classically requires controlling a global oscillation modulus over all nearby triples of times. We prove such an Aldous-type characterisation of $M_1$ tightness, replacing the global modulus condition by local estimates at stopping times ruling out rapid reversals after a large excursion. Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. They reduce the verification of $M_1$ tightness to short-time estimates for the processes restarted from its state at suitable stopping times.

papers.title: Solid-angle formulas for simplicial cones and random shifted sections of polytopes
papers.abstract: We consider simplicial cones $C = \operatorname{pos}(v_1, \ldots, v_n) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose generators have a Gram matrix of the form $(\langle v_i, v_j \rangle)_{i,j=1}^n = \operatorname{Id}_n+\sum_{j=1}^p \lambda_j u_j u_j^T$, where $p\in \{0,\ldots, n\}$, $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p > -1$ and $u_1,\ldots, u_p \in \mathbb{R}^n$ are orthogonal unit vectors. We derive an explicit $p$-dimensional integral formula for the solid angle of $C$ involving the analytic continuation of the standard normal distribution function. As an application, explicit formulas are obtained for the expected face numbers of sections of acute orthocentric simplices and crosspolytopes with uniformly distributed linear subspaces translated by a fixed vector. The translation vector is assumed to lie outside the affine hulls of all proper faces of the polytope. All solid angles entering these formulas are expressed as integrals of dimension at most two. This application includes regular simplices and regular crosspolytopes as special cases.

papers.title: Berry--Esseen Bounds for Faces in Unimodular Triangulations of Random Polytopes
papers.abstract: Consider the number of faces arising from unimodular triangulations of random polytopes associated with Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs. Focusing on two-dimensional faces of regular unimodular triangulations of random symmetric edge polytopes, we derive precise asymptotic expansions for the expectation and variance and then establish a quantitative central limit theorem with an explicit Berry--Esseen bound. The proof combines an algebraically derived characterization of faces in terms of local graph configurations with a detailed combinatorial--geometric study of the relevant configurations. The normal approximation is established using the discrete Malliavin--Stein method. We also determine the asymptotic orders of the expectation and variance and establish a quantitative central limit theorem for the number of faces in each fixed higher dimension. These results identify a common local mechanism underlying the fluctuations of face numbers and extend the distributional theory of random symmetric edge polytopes [Donzelmann et al., arXiv:2603.10650] beyond edge statistics.

papers.title: An exact coexistence criterion for stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems with Volterra--Lyapunov stable interactions
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic Lotka-Volterra systems $dX=\mathrm{Diag}(X)(\alpha+AX)dt+\mathrm{Diag}(X)\Gamma dB$ with nondegenerate noise and a Volterra-Lyapunov stable interaction matrix $A$, that is, $DA+A^\top D\prec 0$ for some positive diagonal matrix $D$. This class covers every self-limited predator-prey food web that is conservative in the sense of Volterra, in particular every such web whose interaction graph is a forest. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for invariant coexistence: the process has an invariant probability measure on $(0,\infty)^n$, that is, a stationary distribution under which all species have positive densities, if and only if $m=-A^{-1}\beta$ is positive, where $\beta=\alpha-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma\Gamma^\top)$ is the vector of noise-corrected growth rates. This measure is then unique and ergodic, has mean $m$, and attracts every interior initial condition exponentially fast in total variation. Thus environmental noise affects coexistence only through the It\^o shift $\alpha\mapsto\beta$, and the criterion is the exact counterpart of the feasibility criterion for the deterministic system $\dot x=\mathrm{Diag}(x)(\beta+Ax)$. Both directions rest on the fact that, for Lotka-Volterra systems, invasion rates are affine in the mean of the underlying measure. Necessity follows from an exact formula for the means of invariant measures supported on faces of the orthant. Sufficiency follows from the persistence theorem of Hening and Nguyen, for which the explicit weights $Dm$ give a stochastic counterpart of Hofbauer's average Lyapunov function, so that no enumeration of the invariant measures on the boundary is required. Applied to subcommunities, the result also characterizes every stationary regime in which some species are absent.

papers.title: Random $C^*$-subalgebras
papers.abstract: Given a discrete countable group $\Gamma$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(\Gamma)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(\Gamma)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $\Gamma$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(\Gamma)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $\Gamma$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$, respectively.
